read.sections.0.heading.source: Change can appear in the background
read.sections.0.heading.back: Change can appear in the background

read.sections.0.text.source:
The history of a new transport system can be told through engineering plans, lists of passengers, buildings or paintings. Each source shows different things. A painting may show how infrastructure, such as railways and bridges, entered the places where people met, waited, travelled or spent their free time. It also shows what the artist decided to emphasise.

Édouard Manet painted The Railway in 1873. A woman faces the viewer while a girl looks through an iron fence. Steam fills much of the space beyond them. The National Gallery of Art explains that the setting is connected with the railway near Manet's studio. Surprisingly, the train that gives the painting its title is not clearly shown as the main subject. People, a barrier and the air around the tracks carry much of the scene.

It would be easy to invent a relationship or a conversation for the figures. The painting alone cannot prove one. The museum's account keeps the models it has identified apart from possible interpretations of the scene. A careful viewer can describe where the figures are looking, while accepting that their thoughts remain unknown.
read.sections.0.text.back:
The history of a new transport system can be told through engineering plans, passenger lists, buildings or paintings. Each source shows different things. A painting can show how infrastructure, such as railways and bridges, entered places where people met, waited, travelled or spent free time. The painting also shows what the artist chose to bring forward.

Édouard Manet painted The Railway in 1873. A woman faces toward the person looking at the painting, while a girl looks beyond an iron fence. Steam fills most of the space behind them. The National Gallery of Art explains that the setting is related to the railway line near Manet's studio. Strangely, the train that gives the painting its title is not clearly shown as its main subject. People, a barrier and the air around the tracks fill most of the scene.

It is very easy to invent a relationship or a conversation for the two figures. The painting itself cannot prove one. The museum's explanation keeps the models it has identified apart from possible interpretations of the scene. A person who looks carefully can describe where the figures are looking, while accepting that their thoughts remain unknown.

read.sections.0.simpler.source:
Plans, lists of passengers, buildings and paintings all tell us about a new railway. Each shows different things. Infrastructure means systems like railways and bridges. A painting can show infrastructure where people met, waited, travelled or rested. It also shows the artist's choices.

Manet painted The Railway in 1873. A woman looks out at us. A girl looks through an iron fence. Steam fills the space behind them. The museum says the place is near a railway by Manet's studio. But we cannot clearly see a train. People, a fence and steam fill most of the picture.

It is easy to make up a story about the two people. But the painting cannot prove one. The museum knows who posed. It keeps that apart from ideas about the scene. We can say where each one looks. We cannot know what they think.
read.sections.0.simpler.back:
Plans, passenger lists, buildings and paintings all tell about a new railway line. Each shows different things. Infrastructure means systems like railways and bridges. A painting can show infrastructure in places where people met, waited, travelled or rested. A painting also shows its artist's choices.

Manet painted The Railway in 1873. A woman looks toward us. A girl looks through an iron fence. Steam fills the space behind them. The museum says the place is near the railway line next to Manet's studio. But we cannot see a train clearly. People, a fence and steam fill most of the picture.

It is easy to make up a story about those two people. But the painting cannot prove it. The museum knows who posed as models. The museum keeps that apart from ideas about the scene. We can say where each one looks. We cannot know what they think.

read.sections.1.text.source:
Claude Monet painted Argenteuil in about 1872. It gives another view of a changing environment. A riverside path, trees, boats, people, buildings and distant smokestacks share the same picture. The scene does not divide nature and human activity into separate worlds. Looking from its foreground to its horizon helps us notice several uses of the landscape at once.

Railways also changed the links between Paris and nearby towns. A teaching resource from the National Gallery of Art, Picturing France, 1830–1900, explains this. Train services tied once-rural settlements more closely to the capital. Homes, industry and leisure grew up alongside each other. Argenteuil became a centre for sailing. Factories also stood by the river in the suburbs, the settlements connected with the city. Train journeys made day trips easier for more city residents. Still, chances and resources remained unequal. Artists could therefore find both recreation and industry in one place.
read.sections.1.text.back:
Claude Monet painted Argenteuil in about 1872. This painting gives another view of an environment that is changing. A path on the riverbank, trees, boats, people, buildings and chimneys in the distance are in the same picture. The scene does not separate nature and human activity into separate worlds. Looking from the foreground to the horizon helps us notice several uses of the landscape at once.

Railway lines also changed the connections between Paris and the towns near it. A teaching resource from the National Gallery of Art, Picturing France, 1830–1900, explains this. Train services tied settlements that used to be rural more closely to the capital. Homes, industry and places to relax grew side by side. Argenteuil became a centre for the sport of sailing boats. Factories also stood on the riverbank in the suburbs, that is, settlements connected with the big city. Train journeys made it easier for more city residents to take a day trip. Even so, chances and resources remained unequal. So artists could find recreation and industry in one place.
read.sections.1.text.note: "suburb" is "pinggiran kota" (the glossary word). "resources" is "sumber daya", as KEY_TERMS.

read.sections.1.simpler.source:
Monet painted Argenteuil in about 1872. It shows a path by a river. There are trees, boats, people and buildings. Far away are tall factory chimneys. Nature and people's work share one picture. It shows many uses of the land at once.

Trains linked Paris with towns near it. Homes, factories and places for fun grew side by side. Argenteuil became a place for sailing. Factories also stood by the river in the suburbs. A suburb is a place linked to a big city. Trains made day trips easier for more people. But not everyone had the same chances or money. So artists found both fun and factories in one place.
read.sections.1.simpler.back:
Monet painted Argenteuil in about 1872. This painting shows a path on a riverbank. There are trees, boats, people and buildings. Far away there are tall factory chimneys. Nature and human work are in one picture. This picture shows many uses of the land at once.

Trains connected Paris with the towns near it. Homes, factories and places to have fun grew side by side. Argenteuil became a place for sailing. Factories also stood on the riverbank in the suburbs. A suburb is a place connected with a big city. Trains made it easy for more people to take a day trip. But not everyone had the same chances or money. So artists found places for fun and factories in one place.

read.sections.2.heading.source: Arguments about what art should be
read.sections.2.heading.back: Arguments about what art should be like

read.sections.2.text.source:
Art institutions also shaped French cultural life. Every year, a jury chose the paintings for the Paris Salon, a large official exhibition. In 1874, Monet and other artists organised their own independent exhibition. It is linked with the start of Impressionism. Their loose brushwork and their attention to modern life challenged ideas about a finished painting. Paris held competing ideas about what art should show and how it should look. National identity did not produce one agreed French style. Institutions, critics, artists and audiences all helped decide which art was recognised.

Studying change through these works combines looking with context. We can explain how a composition, or arrangement of parts, directs attention. We can identify the recorded place and date, and connect the scene to wider developments. This tells us more than calling every part of modernisation simply progress or decline. Modernisation means changes in technology, institutions and ways of life, and it takes different forms.
read.sections.2.text.back:
Art institutions also shaped French cultural life. Every year, a jury chose the paintings for the Paris Salon, a large official exhibition. In 1874, Monet and other artists organised their own independent exhibition. This exhibition is associated with the start of Impressionism. Their loose brushstrokes and their attention to modern life challenged ideas about a finished painting. Paris held competing ideas about what art should show and what it should look like. National identity did not produce one agreed French style. Institutions, critics, artists and audiences all helped decide which art was recognised.

Studying change through these works joins observation with context. We can explain how a composition, or arrangement of parts, directs attention. We can identify the recorded place and date, and connect the scene with wider developments. This tells us more than calling every part of modernisation just progress or decline. Modernisation means changes in technology, institutions and ways of life, and its forms differ.

read.sections.2.simpler.source:
Art groups also mattered in France. Each year, judges picked paintings for a big show in Paris called the Salon. In 1874, Monet and other artists held their own show. It is linked with the start of Impressionism. They painted modern life with loose brush marks. To many people, this did not look finished. So people in Paris did not agree about art. There was not one French style. Judges, critics, artists and viewers all decided which art got praise.

So we look closely and learn the context. A composition is how the parts of a picture are arranged. It guides our eyes. We can find the place and date. We can link the scene to bigger changes. Modernisation means new machines, new groups and new ways of life. It can take many forms. It is not simply good or bad.
read.sections.2.simpler.back:
Art groups were also important in France. Every year, the judges picked paintings for a big exhibition in Paris called the Salon. In 1874, Monet and other artists made their own exhibition. This exhibition is associated with the start of Impressionism. They painted modern life with loose brushstrokes. To many people, the paintings looked unfinished. So people in Paris did not agree about art. There was not one French style. Judges, critics, artists and audiences all decided which art was praised.

So we look carefully and learn its context. A composition is the way the parts of a picture are arranged. A composition guides our eyes. We can find its place and date. We can connect the scene with bigger changes. Modernisation means new machines, new groups and new ways of life. Its forms can be many. Modernisation is not simply good or bad.

write.prompt.back: Choose Manet's or Monet's painting. Explain how that painting connects everyday life with a world of new railways and buildings. Use one detail you can see and one fact from its history.

write.sentenceStarters.0.source: In the painting, I can see ...
write.sentenceStarters.0.back: In the painting, I can see ...

write.example.source: In Monet's Argenteuil, I can see people walking by the river. There are boats on the water and smokestacks far away. The history tells us that trains linked towns like Argenteuil more closely with Paris. People went sailing there, but factories were also built by the river. This shows that rest and industry shared the same landscape. People rested and worked side by side.
write.example.back: In Monet's painting Argenteuil, I can see people walking on the riverbank. There are boats on the water and chimneys far away. Its history tells us that trains brought towns like Argenteuil closer to Paris. People went sailing there, but factories were also built on the riverbank. This shows that rest and industry were in the same landscape. People rested and worked side by side.
